articles.title: The Plan: Architecture Firm Corgan Redesigned Its Own Empire State Building Office
articles.narrative: Architecture firm Corgan has completed a significant renovation and expansion of its New York City office on the 54th floor of the Empire State Building. The firm increased its footprint from 18,714 square feet to 26,035 square feet, accommodating nearly 150 employees in a full-floor space. The redesign, conceptualized as "Echoes of Deco," integrates Art Deco themes and original building elements with modern amenities and a strong focus on sustainability and employee well-being.

data_points.notable_features: Office design incorporates Art Deco themes, original building elements, and modern amenities including a large cafe, 3D model printing shop, media room, phone rooms, mother's room, and wellness room. The project emphasized healthy materials and ESG alignment.
data_points.project_notes: Corgan's aviation, data center, and corporate interiors teams temporarily relocated during the year-long renovation. The office can now accommodate up to 162 employees.

articles.title: Arrow Real Estate Advisors Hires Jeff Weinberg as Managing Director
Alexandria Shows Positive Signs After Several Depressed Quarters: Earnings
articles.narrative: Alexandria Real Estate Equities, a life sciences-focused REIT, reported signs of improvement in the second quarter of 2026, with increased leasing activity despite a decline in net income and funds from operations compared to the previous year. The company leased 1 million square feet of space, a significant increase from the prior quarter, driven by strong demand from life science product, service, and device sectors. Executives expressed optimism about the improving economic conditions in science sectors, anticipating further balance sheet stabilization by 2028.
articles.market_intelligence: Colliers predicted in March 2026 that the remainder of 2026 would be favorable for the life science industry due to increased investment in weight-loss therapy drugs like GLP-1s. There has also been an influx of investment in underperforming life science assets, despite the unlikelihood of conversion to other uses.

articles.title: Munish Viralam of Newmark: 5 Questions
articles.narrative: Munish Viralam, formerly of CBRE, has joined Newmark as Executive Vice Chairman to lead the firm's newly centralized real estate strategy and consulting group. His role involves scaling Newmark's strategic advisory arm and assisting corporate tenants in New York City with their real estate strategies and negotiations. Viralam emphasizes a transactional-based, analytical approach that integrates Newmark's diverse strengths, including corporate advisory, research, workplace strategy, and capital markets, to provide comprehensive long-term occupancy solutions for clients. He notes the strong demand for high-quality office assets in New York City, driven by companies reinvesting in their occupancy post-COVID-19 to attract talent and scale businesses, despite a tight market for such properties.

articles.title: Prologis’ European Rival Segro Accepts $18.8B Takeover Offer
articles.narrative: Prologis, the world's largest industrial landlord, is set to expand its global footprint significantly with the acquisition of Segro, the United Kingdom's largest REIT. The $18.8 billion all-equity deal, which values Segro's equity, will create a combined portfolio of approximately $269 billion in assets under management. Segro's board, after initially resisting three prior offers, has now recommended the acquisition, which is expected to close in the first half of 2027, pending regulatory and shareholder approvals. The acquisition will boost Prologis' European operating portfolio by 47% and its European land bank by 126%, integrating Segro's extensive U.K. and European logistics and data center assets.

data_points.project_notes: The acquisition is expected to close in the first half of 2027, subject to legal, regulatory, and Segro shareholder approvals. Prologis will apply for a secondary listing on the London Stock Exchange as part of the deal.

articles.title: What’s Next for the U.S. Office Market?
articles.narrative: The U.S. office market is showing signs of stabilization after the pandemic-induced downturn, with leasing activity remaining steady in Q2 2026, albeit still below pre-pandemic levels. The national vacancy rate has decreased, and rental rates are increasing, particularly for Class A properties. The "flight to quality" trend continues, with amenity-rich Class A spaces in vibrant neighborhoods attracting tenants, while new construction starts are at a 14-year low, leading to limited availability of large contiguous spaces.

articles.title: JLL Negotiates Sale of 248-Unit Apartment Complex in El Paso
articles.narrative: JLL has negotiated the sale of Palomar West, a 248-unit apartment complex in El Paso, Texas. The property, built in 1986, features one- and two-bedroom units and amenities such as a pool, fitness center, and resident clubhouse. Dallas-based Saxony Capital Management was the seller in this transaction.

data_points.notable_features: Amenities include a pool, fitness center, and resident clubhouse.

articles.title: PNC Bank Provides Financing for Three Affordable Housing Properties Totaling 224 Units in Kerrville, Texas
articles.narrative: PNC Bank has provided financing for three affordable housing properties in Kerrville, Texas, totaling 224 units. This funding is part of a larger $251 million initiative by PNC to support the development, rehabilitation, and preservation of 16 affordable housing properties across the United States, encompassing approximately 1,700 units.

articles.title: Versal Negotiates Sale of 93-Unit Self-Storage Facility in The Colony, Texas
articles.narrative: Versal, a self-storage brokerage firm, has facilitated the sale of a 93-unit self-storage facility in The Colony, Texas. The property, totaling 9,300 net rentable square feet, is operated by LifeSmart Storage. Both the seller and the buyer were Texas-based limited liability companies.

articles.title: Walker & Dunlop Arranges $137.5M Loan for Refinancing of Brooklyn Apartment Building
articles.narrative: Walker & Dunlop has arranged a $137.5 million floating-rate loan for the refinancing of 12 Halsey, a 240-unit apartment building in Brooklyn's Bedford-Stuyvesant neighborhood. The property, completed last fall, includes 30 percent affordable housing units and features a strong amenity package. The loan was secured through AllianceBernstein for the ownership partnership of EJS Group and Hope Street Capital.

data_points.notable_features: 30 percent of units are reserved as affordable housing. Amenities include a pool, fitness center, rooftop terraces, coworking space, and outdoor grilling and dining stations. The building also includes 2,400 square feet of ground-floor retail space.

articles.title: Transwestern: Chicago’s suburban office market is in recovery mode, but that recovery is slow
articles.narrative: A recent report on Chicago's suburban office market indicates a slow but positive recovery, with 106,407 square feet of positive net absorption in the second quarter of 2026. This improvement was primarily driven by limited tenant movement and renewals rather than new leasing activity, as evidenced by a significant renewal by a major pharmaceutical company and a food ingredient supplier. Despite elevated vacancy rates, average asking rents have shown resilience, increasing to $27.16 per square foot. Investment activity is focused on redevelopment and conversion opportunities for obsolete office properties, with minimal new construction observed.
articles.market_intelligence: Chicago's suburban office market posted 106,407 square feet of positive net absorption in Q2 2026, with all five submarkets recording gains. The direct vacant available rate fell 75 basis points to 18.8%, while the broader availability rate inched up to 25.8%. Average full-service asking rents rose to $27.16 per square foot, an 80 basis point increase year-over-year. The O'Hare submarket had the highest average asking rent at $32.52 per square foot. No suburban office buildings larger than 40,000 square feet were under construction in Q2 2026.

articles.title: Krusinski Construction Company completes tenant build-out at Hutchins distribution center
articles.narrative: Krusinski Construction Company completed a tenant build-out for a new occupant at the IAC – Wintergreen development in Hutchins, Texas. The tenant now occupies the remaining 266,788 square feet within the distribution center.

articles.title: SR Realty Trust acquires 183,000-square-foot distribution facility in Whitestown
articles.narrative: SR Realty Trust has acquired Westpark Logistics Center, a newly constructed 183,000-square-foot Class-A industrial distribution facility in Whitestown, Indiana. The property is fully leased to a regional coffee chain, serving as a critical distribution hub for over 300 locations. This acquisition marks SR Realty Trust's entry into the Indianapolis market, strategically expanding its Midwest portfolio.

data_points.notable_features: Class-A industrial distribution facility with immediate access to Interstate 65 and proximity to Interstate 465.

articles.market_intelligence: Whitestown, IN is one of the fastest-growing industrial submarkets in the Indianapolis metropolitan area, attracting national distribution, logistics, and manufacturing users due to its strategic location, skilled workforce, and business-friendly environment.

articles.title: Irgens starts construction on 204-unit apartment community in Wauwatosa
articles.narrative: Irgens has commenced construction on Viridia Apartments, a 204-unit market-rate apartment community in Wauwatosa, marking the company's entry into multifamily development. The four-story project is situated at a prominent address on West Wisconsin Avenue.

data_points.project_notes: This is Irgens' first multifamily development.

articles.narrative: The New York City Taxi and Limousine Commission (TLC) has signed a 39,000-square-foot lease at 250 Broadway for its new headquarters, with occupancy anticipated in the first quarter of 2027. This transaction expands AmTrustRE's existing relationship with the City of New York, underscoring the building's appeal to institutional tenants due to its prime location and modern infrastructure.

articles.title: Co-Living Complex Near UCLA Will Become Student Housing
articles.narrative: A seven-story co-living complex in West Los Angeles, near UCLA, has been sold for $8.5 million to UCLA Housing Group, which plans to convert it into student housing. The property, built in 2023, features 16 residential units and 48 beds across 18,000 square feet. The transaction, completed through a court-appointed receivership, reflects a broader market trend in Los Angeles where investors are acquiring existing assets below replacement cost due to muted rent growth and increasing development challenges.

data_points.notable_features: Seven-story, Type II co-living property located near UCLA.
data_points.project_notes: Sale completed through a court-appointed receivership process. Buyer plans to convert the property into student housing.

articles.market_intelligence: The Los Angeles multifamily market has experienced muted rent growth post-pandemic, while household incomes, replacement costs, and home prices have increased. New development has become more challenging, leading investors to focus on acquiring well-located existing assets below replacement cost.

articles.title: Development Site with Uncommonly Long Frontage Sells in Brooklyn
articles.narrative: A residential development site with significant frontage in Brooklyn's Bedford-Stuyvesant neighborhood has been sold for $23.5 million. The 26,730-square-foot corner parcel, located at 1150 Broadway, was acquired by YS Developers and Rabsky Group from A-PLUS International Realty. The site offers substantial development potential, with zoning for a mixed-use building up to 133,917 square feet, and benefits from its location within a Qualified Opportunity Zone and eligibility for the 485-x tax abatement program. The property's extensive wraparound frontage and direct subway access were key factors in attracting strong developer interest.

data_points.notable_features: Features approximately 475 feet of wraparound frontage along Lafayette Avenue, Kosciuszko Street, Kossuth Place and Broadway; located at the crossroads of Bedford-Stuyvesant and Bushwick with direct subway access.
data_points.project_notes: Zoned for a mixed-use building with apartments, local retail and community facilities; offers up to 133,917 square feet of as-of-right zoning floor area under the City of Yes for Housing Opportunity program; sits within a federally designated Qualified Opportunity Zone and is eligible for the 485-x tax abatement program.

articles.title: Triple-Net AutoZone Sells to Private Investor from LA
articles.narrative: A renovated, single-tenant AutoZone property in Bakersfield, CA, has been sold for $2.64 million to a private investor from Los Angeles. The property, which underwent a full renovation in 2025, is secured by a new 15-year triple-net lease with AutoZone. The sale highlights strong investor demand for essential retail assets in rapidly expanding suburban markets, particularly for properties with long-term leases and investment-grade tenants.

data_points.notable_features: Renovated in 2025 and leased on a new 15-year triple-net lease.
data_points.project_notes: Buyer was an all-cash 1031-exchange buyer from Nevada.

articles.title: Alexandria's $73M Quarterly Loss Highlights Deepening Life Sciences Real Estate Slump
articles.narrative: Alexandria Real Estate Equities reported a significant net loss of $73.7 million in the second quarter, reflecting the ongoing downturn in the life sciences real estate market. This quarterly performance underscores the broader challenges facing the sector, including reduced demand and increased vacancies, which are impacting the financial health of major players in the space.

articles.title: PRP Buys Downtown Office Building From Tishman Speyer
articles.narrative: PRP, an investment firm, has acquired the office building at 900 19th St. NW in Washington, D.C., from Tishman Speyer for $30 million. The new owner plans to implement upgrades to the property.

articles.title: The World's Largest Data Center Hub Pursues A Development Pause. Is It Even Legal?
articles.narrative: Loudoun County is currently debating a temporary halt on new data center development applications, despite the fact that such moratoriums are explicitly illegal under Virginia state law. This move comes as the county, home to the world's largest data center hub, grapples with the rapid expansion of these facilities and their associated infrastructure demands. The legal implications of pursuing a development pause in contravention of state statutes are a central point of contention in the ongoing discussions.

articles.title: New York Investor Buys Smyrna Flex Warehouse
articles.narrative: LM Real Estate Partners has acquired the 3M industrial property in Smyrna for $27 million. This transaction reflects a significant 40% increase in value for the flex warehouse asset.

articles.title: The World Cup Boosted LA Hotel Rates. Occupancy Barely Budged
articles.narrative: The World Cup significantly increased hotel rates in Los Angeles, but this surge in pricing did not translate into a notable rise in occupancy. The article suggests that high travel costs and intense competition among event planners contributed to the stagnant occupancy levels despite the major international event.
